Guidance & outlook: India's real GDP growth for FY2025-26 is estimated at 7.6% (FY2024-25: 7.1%), supported by government capital expenditure, resilient private consumption, and steady performance across the manufacturing and services sectors.
India's economic outlook for FY2026-27 remains positive, with the RBI projecting real GDP growth of approximately 6.9% and CPI inflation of around 4.6%.

Importantly, supply additions remained measured - ICRA projects demand growth of 8-10% CAGR against supply growth of only 5-6% over FY2025-FY2028 - a demand-supply imbalance that is expected to sustain occupancy and pricing, including across select Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets where your Company has historically concentrated its presence.
Growth & demand: Services remained the primary engine of growth, expanding by an estimated 8.7% and contributing approximately 55- 60% of Gross Value Added.

Within services, ‘Trade, Hotels, Transport, Communication and Broadcasting Services' - the segment most directly relevant to your Company - grew by around 10.1%, while ‘Financial, Real Estate and Professional Services' grew by 9.9%.

Manufacturing is estimated to have grown by 11.5% (FY2024-25: 9.3%), supported by production-linked incentive schemes and steady domestic demand, while construction grew at 7.1% and agriculture at 2.4%, aided by an above-normal monsoon.
Margins & costs: COST AUDITORS The provisions of Section 148 of the Companies Act, 2013, regarding the maintenance of cost records and mandatory cost audit are not applicable to the Company.
Inflationary pressures moderated during the year, with CPI inflation remaining broadly within the RBI's tolerance band of 4% ± 2%, aided by easing food prices.

DISCUSSION ON FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE WITH RESPECT TO OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE During FY 2025-26, The Byke achieved a revenue of ₹106.69 crore from its hotel operations, along with an EBITDA of ₹670.45 crore (reflecting an EBITDA margin of 6.28%) and a Profit After Tax of ₹6.70 crore, delivering a PAT margin of 6.28%.
Capex & expansion: We recently strengthened this footprint through new property acquisitions in metropolitan areas, and continue to invest in technology, with our in-house revenue management system, Revyog, progressing steadily towards profitability.
The Company held cash and cash equivalents of ₹ 3.97 crore at the end of the year, providing a comfortable liquidity buffer to support operations and fund planned expansion.

RESOURCES AND LIQUIDITY As of March 31, 2026, the Company's net worth stood at ₹ 231.47 crore, while total debt was: ₹ 16.75 crore.

According to the information and explanations given to us and based on our verification of the records, the Company has been sanctioned working capital limits in excess of ₹5 crores in aggregate from banks on the basis of security of current assets.
Risks & challenges: The Company has adopted Risk Management Policy, pursuant to the provision of Section 134 of the Act, to identify and evaluate business risks and approach for mitigation of such risks.

Our Board-level risk management committee closely monitors the framework, and we regularly review performance and adjust internal processes to stay ahead of emerging challenges. by identifying and addressing potential risks quickly, we protect what we have built, sharpen our competitive edge, and make better strategic decisions.
